narrative:
The Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 49.1% on September 29, 2026, with 1,440 cases heard out of 2,933 scheduled. This marks a notable rise in efficiency from the previous day, September 28, when the court achieved a 45.5% hearing rate, resolving 1,382 out of 3,039 scheduled matters. 

Individual performance highlights include Justice T.P. Vivekananda in Hall 36, who maintained high disposal rates by hearing 45 out of 53 scheduled cases (84.9%), sustaining a strong performance level from the prior day's 82.4% rate. The division bench of the Chief Justice & K.S. Hemalekha in Hall 1 also recorded high conversion in one of their sessions, hearing 22 out of 25 cases (88.0%). Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde in Hall 26 heard 40 out of 51 cases (78.4%) in his primary block, while Justice S.R. Krishna Kumar in Hall 12 resolved 57 out of 89 scheduled matters (64.0%).

In terms of hearing stages, Orders dominated the docket with 868 scheduled and 488 heard (56.2%), a rise in conversion efficiency from the 52.7% recorded on September 28. Preliminary Hearings achieved a 52.4% conversion rate (239 heard of 456), while Final Hearings converted at 32.0%, showing moderate progress compared to the previous day's 28.0%. Writ Petitions (WP) constituted the largest case category with 1,336 scheduled matters and an improved conversion rate of 47.9% compared to 45.4% yesterday. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) and Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) followed, converting at 48.8% and 48.5% respectively, representing steady clearance across major case categories.
